NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular
  business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a
  recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35
  (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

A.  ELECTRONIC BICYCLE (E-BIKE) UPDATE AND CONSIDERATIONS

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive this report and discuss the topic of
  e-bikes and provide policy direction to City staff.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER thanked Management Analyst Slawson for a
comprehensive report. Management Analyst Slawson explained the School District’s position
in promoting safety and noted that do not handle any type of enforcement at this time, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER. COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER
complimented the mobile signage that has been installed, stated that two have disappeared,
and enquired about making them more permanent.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER inquired if the Sheriff can identify the types of electric
bicycles (e-bikes), or if their focus is just on the speed of the e-bikes. Management Analyst
Slawson explained that the Sheriff’s Department enforces the California Vehicle Code (CVC)
pertaining to the roadway, not the trails and pathways, and that there can be difficulty in
enforcement on the trails.

Management Analyst Slawson explained that many cities do not require registration because
of the cost of implementation and enforcement and found that some cities are removing
registration from their municipal codes, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER who
inquired about the possibility of e-bike registration.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA expressed concern about young riders who do not know the
rules of the road, who ride recklessly without helmets on the multi-use paths. She believes all

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 24, 2023
 the uses of e-bikes can coexist, if they are regulated in a way that promotes safety such as:
class 3 riders must be 16 years or older; lower-level bike riders must wear a helmet if under
17. She would like the City to work with the School District and other stakeholders to introduce
voluntary safe riding technique classes with certificates, to provide some practical knowledge
about the rules of the road and how to safely use these powerful bikes. She suggested using
e-bike registration as a tool to recover stolen bicycles, which is being done in Davis, California.
She stated that she is not seeking to prohibit the use of e-bikes in the City but is seeking to
introduce some commonsense regulations that promote safety, especially for young riders who
do not yet know the rules of the road.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN agreed with everything said by his fellow Council Members,
and asked the City Attorney how much leeway the City has in terms of regulating e-bikes on
registration, use of helmets etc. City Attorney Davis stated that some of the general health and
safety items would be within the City’s purview, such as helmet wearing, requiring use of
separate seats, or registration, but that requiring speed limits would be a different discussion.
COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN agreed that helmets should be required for riders under the
age of 16. He noted that there are good uses for e-bikes, and wants to explore ideas regarding
education, and suggested other organizations such as AYSO or Little Leagues also help
promote education.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER stated that some riders are using the trails for recreation
rather than transportation even though it is not allowed.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested raising the fines to dissuade people from riding
e-bikes on the trails.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ talked about E-Bike Sense who has a contract with Hermosa
Valley Unified School District, who provides a 2-hour e-bike safety training course. She agreed
with COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN that if we don’t have a large enough fine, it won’t
prevent people from riding e-bikes on the trails.

Discussion ensued about bike shop manufacturers locally and online, and their responsibility
in education. Assistant City Manager Davis noted that a local e-bike shop in the City is looking
into providing educational workshops.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that the law states type-3 e-bikes are not supposed to
be used by riders under the age of 16. She summarized other laws as outlined in the table
attached to the staff report.

City Manager Grammer summarized the direction to staff from the City Council. He expressed
concern about permanent signage getting lost in the background, whereas mobile signage can
be moved around to various locations and may be more noticeable. He suggested keeping
them mobile for now since it is a new program, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
SCHACHTER.

City Manager Grammer stated that staff has budgeted for a changeable message board, and
plans on purchasing one this year which can display messaging about prohibiting e-bikes on
the City’s trails, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’s suggestion.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE REPORT, AND DIRECT STAFF TO CONTINUE
  EDUCATION AND OUTREACH REGARDING E-BIKE REGULATIONS AND
  SAFETY, PARTNER WITH THE SCHOOL DISTRICT AND LOCAL E-BIKE
  SHOP REGARDING COMMUNITY EDUCATION, CONTINUE TO WORK
  WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY SHERIFF’S DEPARTMENT
  REGARDING ENFORCEMENT, INCREASE EDUCATION ON CURRENT
  STATE AND LOCAL LAWS REGARDING E-BIKES, RETURN TO COUNCIL

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 24, 2023
   WITH CURRENT FINES AND OPTIONS TO INCREASE THEM ALONG WITH
  POTENTIAL MUNICIPAL CODE UPDATES.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

B.  WESTFIELD PROPERTY OWNERS’ ASSOCIATION LICENSE AGREEMENT FOR
  PRIVATE SECURITY CAMERA EQUIPMENT LOCATED ON CITY PROPERTY

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Westfield Property Owners
  Association License Agreement as to form by the City Attorney for Private Security
  Camera Equipment Located on City Property which will allow neighborhood cameras to
  be installed on City rights-of-way.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA clarified that it is a security camera and license plate reading
camera.

Management Analyst Slawson explained that the homeowner’s association (HOA) will be
responsible for monitoring the camera data, but as part of the grant program, the City requires
the HOA share the camera data with the Sheriff’s Department, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER SCHACHTER.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

 12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR HUFF stated there is renewed interest to discuss gas-powered leaf blowers. City
Manager Grammer suggested the item be brought to the Environmental Advisory Committee
for discussion.

MAYOR HUFF reported that on October 13-15 was the annual Tracy Austin Doubles Tennis
Tournament which was a hugely successful event with a record number of participants. She
also reported that this past weekend was the Prepared Peninsula Expo and Natural Disaster

a well-attended event and thanked the City’s community partners for participating to help the
community learn about preparing and planning for disasters. She noted there was a helpful
PowerPoint presentation that was presented, which will be available on the City’s website, and
